Operations Runbook: Waypoint Dispatch

Waypoint Field Service Platform is the product our dispatch and field teams run on every day. It bundles two customer-facing services into one subscription: Scheduling & Dispatch and Work Order Management.

The Regional Operations Manager, a business actor covering the region, is assigned to the Dispatcher role during a call-out or a busy morning -- never to the Field Technician role, which is a separate assignment reserved for field crew. The Dispatcher role is the one who actually performs the Work Order Fulfillment process -- walking a job from "customer called" to "technician on site" to "invoice sent."

Work Order Fulfillment kicks off the moment a Customer Reports an Issue: that business event triggers the whole process. Most of those reports still come in through the Dispatch Call Center, a business interface staffed during business hours; a call landing there triggers Work Order Fulfillment just as reliably as a report submitted through the app.

Once a job is scheduled, the Field Technician role performs Route Optimization -- a function, not a process, because there's no single finish line; it's an ongoing capability the role exercises on every run, sequencing stops to minimize drive time between jobs. Route Optimization realizes the Scheduling & Dispatch service: the service exists, from the customer's point of view, because that underlying capability keeps it running efficiently.

Work Order Fulfillment itself realizes the Work Order Management service -- the process is how the service actually gets delivered, even though customers only ever see the service, never the process behind it.

Every customer account is covered by a Service Level Agreement, a contract that governs the Work Order Management service: it's what obligates us to a same-day response window. The Waypoint Field Service Platform product composes that contract and aggregates both of the services above -- Scheduling & Dispatch and Work Order Management ship together under one subscription.

Ultimately, the Dispatcher role serves our Customers -- the stakeholder whose experience the whole operation exists to protect. Work Order Fulfillment realizes a specific goal on our roadmap, On-Time Service Delivery, and the Scheduling & Dispatch service satisfies a requirement that goal depends on: Real-Time Technician Location Visibility, without which a dispatcher can't tell a customer an honest ETA.
